TRI-DENT, an innovative automated data generation pipeline that minimizes human intervention. TRI-DENT employs a zero-shot approach using a chat-LLM to generate diverse personas and attributes, which then guide instruction generation.
outputs: harmful instructions paired with safe, aligned responses
The paper generates harmful instructions and corresponding safe, helpful responses for LLM safety alignment.

quote: a series of measures are employed, including average tokens, TTR, ATTR, MATTR, LDI, Self-BLEU, Entropy, Inertia

We use a series of measures ... TTR, ATTR, MATTR, LDI, Self-BLEU, Entropy, Inertia ... to evaluate lexical diversity, and we evaluate model safety using Harm Score, Attack Success Rate, and Helpful Rate.

To evaluate the lexical diversity, a series of measures are employed, including average tokens, TTR(Type-Token Ratio), ATTR(Advanced Type-Token Ratio), MATTR(Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio), LDI(Lexical Diversity Index), Self-BLEU(Self-Bilingual Evaluation Understudy), Entropy, Inertia, as well as BERT-based t-SNE dimensionality reduction methods.
evaluated using GPT-4O-MINI based on four key safety and helpfulness metrics: Harm Score (HS), Attack Success Rate (ASR), Helpful Rate (HPR)
We use GPT-4O-MINI to evaluate the generated responses based on four key safety and helpfulness metrics: Harm Score, Attack Success Rate, Helpful Rate, and Helpful Rate.

We use instructions from redteaming datasets to prompt LLMs and generate responses, which are evaluated using GPT-4O-MINI based on four key safety and helpfulness metrics: Harm Score (HS): Measures the harmfulness of responses on a scale from 1 (harmless) to 5 (extremely harmful), following . Attack Success Rate (ASR): Indicates the proportion of responses with HS = 5 (extremely harmful) relative to total attempts, as defined in . Helpful Rate (HPR): Represents the percentage of red-teaming instructions that result in non-refusal responses.
